newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's rice traders await news of Manila deal.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's rice traders await news of Manila deal.

text.p: Vietnam's export rice market was quiet on Thursday as traders awaited final confirmation of a rice deal with the Philippines and as state media remained silent on the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
Dealers said five percent broken grade rice had remained unchanged over the last week at around $270 per tonne FOB Saigon Port. Ten percent broken was quoted at $265.
News of the death of China's Deng Xiaoping late on Wednesday had not been released by Vietnam's communist authorities on Thursday morning.
Despite the official silence, traders contacted by Reuters were aware of the news and said it was having no impact so far on the market.
Dealers said they were more concerned about an agreement between Hanoi and Manila for the Philippines to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from Vietnam.

A preliminary accord was reached earlier this week but traders said they were awaiting the conclusion of the contract, which would give Manila the right to buy 100,000 tonnes of Vietnamese white rice initially, with an option to buy a further 100,000 tonnes at a later date.
